name: Art you can see (Cleveland Museum of Art)
description: 246 picture questions about highlighted works in the Cleveland Museum of Art's open-access (CC0) collection, written by Claude from the museum's own records.

source.name: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access API
source.attribution: Cleveland Museum of Art, Open Access

items.question: Who painted this portrait of a woman in a turquoise gown seated before a golden, flower-patterned wall?
items.explain: The museum record lists this 1882–83 oil on canvas, Portrait of Dora Wheeler, as by the American painter William Merritt Chase (1849–1916).

source.title: Portrait of Dora Wheeler, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: A woman in a shimmering turquoise satin dress sits in a dark wooden chair with her cheek resting on her hand, beside a large glass vase of yellow flowers in front of a gold wall decorated with small flowers and butterflies.
picture.credit: William Merritt Chase (American, 1849–1916), Portrait of Dora Wheeler, 1882–83. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: Who painted this dark, energetic 1909 scene of two fighters grappling in a ring as a crowd looks on?
items.explain: The record identifies Stag at Sharkey's (1909, oil on canvas) as the work of the American artist George Bellows (1882–1925).

source.title: Stag at Sharkey's, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: Two shirtless men lock together in mid-motion inside a roped ring while a referee leans in and a shadowy crowd watches from below.
picture.credit: George Bellows (American, 1882–1925), Stag at Sharkey's, 1909. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: Who painted this calm river scene of two rowers in a racing shell passing a blue flag, made in 1873?
items.explain: The record lists The Biglin Brothers Turning the Stake (1873, oil on canvas) as by the American painter Thomas Eakins (1844–1916).

source.title: The Biglin Brothers Turning the Stake, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: Two men in blue headscarves row a long, narrow wooden boat across a wide river, passing a tall pole with a dark blue flag, with other rowers and spectators in the distance.
picture.credit: Thomas Eakins (American, 1844–1916), The Biglin Brothers Turning the Stake, 1873. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: Who or what is the galloping rider on the pale horse in this eerie, moonlit-looking painting?
items.explain: The work's title is The Race Track (Death on a Pale Horse), so the rider is Death. It is an oil painting by Albert Pinkham Ryder, c. 1896–1908.

source.title: The Race Track (Death on a Pale Horse), Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: A skeletal figure holding a curved scythe rides a pale horse along a curving fence track under a dark, cloudy sky, with a snake in the lower left corner.
picture.credit: Albert Pinkham Ryder (American, 1847–1917), The Race Track (Death on a Pale Horse), c. 1896–1908. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: Which American artist painted this glowing red sunset over a wilderness lake in 1860?
items.explain: The record lists Twilight in the Wilderness (1860, oil on canvas) as by the American painter Frederic Edwin Church (1826–1900).

source.title: Twilight in the Wilderness, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: A fiery red and orange sky with patches of turquoise glows above dark forested hills and a still lake, with bare trees framing the right side.
picture.credit: Frederic Edwin Church (American, 1826–1900), Twilight in the Wilderness, 1860. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: Which French Impressionist painted this view of a woman in a red hood seen through a snowy window with billowing curtains?
items.explain: The record lists The Red Kerchief (c. 1868–73, oil on fabric) as by the French painter Claude Monet (1840–1926).

source.title: The Red Kerchief, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: Looking through a gray doorway with pale curtains pulled aside, a figure in a bright red hood and dark coat stands outside in a snowy garden.
picture.credit: Claude Monet (French, 1840–1926), The Red Kerchief, c. 1868–73. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: Who painted this 1817 scene of the winged Cupid and the sleeping Psyche on a richly decorated couch?
items.explain: The record identifies Cupid and Psyche (1817, oil on canvas) as the work of the French painter Jacques-Louis David (1748–1825).

source.title: Cupid and Psyche, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: A smiling nude winged young man sits on a gilded couch with stars on its base, while a sleeping nude woman with wings reclines against him, with a red canopy and a mountain view behind.
picture.credit: Jacques-Louis David (French, 1748–1825), Cupid and Psyche, 1817. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: Which Italian Renaissance painter made this 1533–34 portrait of a bearded man in a fur-trimmed black coat gesturing on a balcony?
items.explain: The record lists Portrait of a Man, Possibly Girolamo Rosati (1533–34, oil on canvas) as by the Italian painter Lorenzo Lotto (1480–1556).

source.title: Portrait of a Man, Possibly Girolamo Rosati, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: A bearded man in a black cap and dark fur-trimmed clothes with a gold chain raises one hand while resting the other on a blue-draped table, with a stone balustrade and blue sky behind him.
picture.credit: Lorenzo Lotto (Italian, 1480–1556), Portrait of a Man, Possibly Girolamo Rosati, 1533–34. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: What is the relationship between the two people embracing in this oval portrait from around 1770?
items.explain: The title is Elizabeth Shewell West and Her Son, Raphael. Benjamin West painted it around 1770.

source.title: Elizabeth Shewell West and Her Son, Raphael, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: A dark-haired woman in a brown headscarf and green embroidered wrap holds a young child in a white shirt close, with their cheeks touching, within a dark oval.
picture.credit: Benjamin West (American, born The Thirteen Colonies, 1738–1820), Elizabeth Shewell West and Her Son, Raphael, c. 1770. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: Which Dutch master painted this lively 1634 portrait of a smiling man in black with a wide white collar?
items.explain: The record lists Portrait of Tieleman Roosterman (1634, oil on canvas) as by the Dutch painter Frans Hals (c. 1581–1666).

source.title: Portrait of Tieleman Roosterman, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: A man with a mustache and pointed beard, wearing black clothes and a broad white collar, stands with one hand on his hip and the other holding a glove, looking out with a cheerful expression.
picture.credit: Frans Hals (Dutch, c. 1581–1666), Portrait of Tieleman Roosterman, 1634. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: Which Bible story is shown in this Florentine painting of a bearded man with a knife, a kneeling nude youth and an angel flying in?
items.explain: The painting, by Andrea del Sarto, c. 1527, is titled The Sacrifice of Isaac.

source.title: The Sacrifice of Isaac, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: An older man in a red cloak raises a blade while gripping a kneeling, bound nude youth, as a winged child-like angel swoops in from above, with a landscape and a ram behind.
picture.credit: Andrea del Sarto (Italian, 1486–1530), The Sacrifice of Isaac, c. 1527. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: Which German Renaissance artist painted this crowded 1540 hunting scene with a white castle on the hill?
items.explain: The record lists Hunting near Hartenfels Castle (1540) as by the German artist Lucas Cranach (1472–1553).

source.title: Hunting near Hartenfels Castle, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: Hunters on foot and horseback with many dogs chase deer, boar and bears through a forest and across a river, while elegantly dressed spectators watch from a boat and a white castle sits on a hill above.
picture.credit: Lucas Cranach (German, 1472–1553), Hunting near Hartenfels Castle, 1540. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: Which French painter made this calm 1648 scene of the Holy Family seated on classical steps?
items.explain: The record lists The Holy Family on the Steps (1648, oil on canvas) as by the French painter Nicolas Poussin (1594–1665).

source.title: The Holy Family on the Steps, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: A woman in red and blue holds a child on stone steps while another child offers an apple, with an older woman and a man nearby, an orange tree, a fountain basin and classical columns behind.
picture.credit: Nicolas Poussin (French, 1594–1665), The Holy Family on the Steps, 1648. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: Which Italian master, famous for dramatic light and shadow, painted this 1606–7 crucifixion made in Naples?
items.explain: The record lists The Crucifixion of Saint Andrew (1606–7, Naples, oil on canvas) as by the Italian painter Caravaggio (1571–1610).

source.title: The Crucifixion of Saint Andrew, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: A bearded, thin man is tied by his arms and feet to a large wooden cross while a man on a ladder-like step works at the ropes and onlookers, one in armor, gaze up out of the darkness.
picture.credit: Caravaggio (Italian, 1571–1610), The Crucifixion of Saint Andrew, 1606–7. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: What event does this glowing 1835 painting by J. M. W. Turner show?
answers: The burning of the Houses of Lords and Commons
items.correct: The burning of the Houses of Lords and Commons
items.explain: The title is The Burning of the Houses of Lords and Commons, 16 October 1834, painted by the British artist J. M. W. Turner in 1835.

source.title: The Burning of the Houses of Lords and Commons, 16 October 1834, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: Bright orange flames and smoke blaze above a many-arched bridge and a wide river, with the fire reflected in the water and small boats and crowds in the foreground.
picture.credit: Joseph Mallord William Turner (British, 1775–1851), The Burning of the Houses of Lords and Commons, 16 October 1834, 1835. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: Which Dutch artist painted this swirling, brightly colored 1889 view of huge plane trees and road menders?
items.explain: The record lists The Large Plane Trees (Road Menders at Saint-Rémy), 1889, as by the Dutch painter Vincent van Gogh (1853–1890).

source.title: The Large Plane Trees (Road Menders at Saint-Rémy), Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: Massive, twisting tree trunks outlined in dark strokes rise over piles of stones and workers, with a yellow building, a street lamp and two figures on the left in thick, swirling brushwork.
picture.credit: Vincent van Gogh (Dutch, 1853–1890), The Large Plane Trees (Road Menders at Saint-Rémy), 1889. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: Which flowering pond plant fills this large, hazy purple-and-green painting by Claude Monet?
items.explain: The painting, by Claude Monet, c. 1915–26, is titled Water Lilies (Agapanthus).

source.title: Water Lilies (Agapanthus), Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: A wide, misty canvas of soft purple, blue and green strokes with small pale floating blossoms and pads scattered across a watery surface.
picture.credit: Claude Monet (French, 1840–1926), Water Lilies (Agapanthus), c. 1915–26. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: Who painted this 1847 genre scene of men listening to a fiddler in a barn doorway?
items.explain: The record lists The Power of Music (1847, oil on canvas) as by the American painter William Sidney Mount (1807–1868).

source.title: The Power of Music, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: A young man plays a violin inside a barn while two men listen, and in the foreground a man in patched overalls leans on the door, holding a hat and looking down.
picture.credit: William Sidney Mount (American, 1807–1868), The Power of Music, 1847. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: Which material was inlaid into the wood of this extraordinary tea table, alongside bone or ivory and metal?
items.explain: The record says the table is inlaid wood with gilded bronze mounts and inlays of ivory or bone, metal, and mother-of-pearl. Carlo Bugatti made it in Paris, c. 1907.

source.title: Tea Table, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: A curved-legged wooden table with gilded metal feet shaped like hooves or claws, small pale inlays along its frame, and a brass tray on top with horn-shaped ornaments.
picture.credit: Carlo Bugatti (Italian, 1856–1940), Tea Table, c. 1907. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: From which region and period does this bronze of a dancing god in a ring of flames come?
items.explain: The record lists this bronze Nataraja, Shiva as the Lord of Dance, from South India, Tamil Nadu, Chola period (900–1200s), made in the 1000s.

source.title: Nataraja, Shiva as the Lord of Dance, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: A four-armed bronze figure balances on one leg on a small base, the other leg raised, inside a large circular frame edged with small flame shapes.
picture.credit: Nataraja, Shiva as the Lord of Dance, 1000s. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: This ancient Greek-style mixing vessel, with its flaring body and two upswept handles, belongs to which culture?
items.explain: The museum record identifies it as a red-figure calyx-krater by the Policoro Painter, South Italian, Lucanian, made around 400 BCE.

source.title: Red-Figure Calyx-Krater (Mixing Vessel): Medea in Chariot (A); Telephos with Baby Orestes (B), Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: A black vessel with a wide flaring mouth and two curved handles, painted in orange-red with a figure in a sunburst circle and winged figures around it.
picture.credit: Policoro Painter (South Italian, Lucanian, active c. 400 BCE), Red-Figure Calyx-Krater (Mixing Vessel): Medea in Chariot (A); Telephos with Baby Orestes (B), c. 400 BCE. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: What materials make up this footed bowl, whose surface is covered with tiny figures and flowing script?
items.explain: The record gives the technique as brass inlaid with silver. The cup is from Seljuq-period Iran.

source.title: The Wade Cup with Animated Script, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: A deep, round, footed metal bowl in brownish tones with dense engraved patterns, small figures, and bright patches of inlay.
picture.credit: The Wade Cup with Animated Script, 1200–1221. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: This tiny, castle-like Gothic structure with enamel panels, towers and lion heads was made in which place?
items.explain: The record lists this Table Fountain as made in Paris, France, around 1320–40, of gilt-silver and translucent enamels.

source.title: Table Fountain, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: A gilded, multi-tiered miniature building with turrets, pointed arches, small bells and green enamel panels, standing on slender columns.
picture.credit: Table Fountain, c. 1320–40. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: Which animal sits beside the elderly saint in this candlelit painting?
items.explain: The painting is Georges de La Tour's Saint Peter Repentant, from 1645. The rooster appears next to the saint.

source.title: Saint Peter Repentant, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: An old bearded man in dark robes sits with clasped hands and looks upward, lit by a lantern, with a small animal on a ledge beside him.
picture.credit: Georges de La Tour (French, 1593–1652), Saint Peter Repentant, 1645. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: From which country does this group of three seated figures on lotus bases, cast in bronze, come?
items.explain: The record identifies the Amitabha Triad as Korean, from the Joseon dynasty, 1400s, in bronze with traces of gilding.

source.title: Amitabha Triad, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: Three seated bronze figures on lotus-shaped seats joined by curving stems, the center one larger with a rounded topknot.
picture.credit: Amitabha Triad, 1400s. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: What material is this hooded, mourning figure carved from?
items.explain: The record gives the technique as vizille alabaster. Claus de Werve made it for the tomb of Philip the Bold.

source.title: Mourner from the Tomb of Philip the Bold, Duke of Burgundy (1364–1404), Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: A pale standing figure wrapped in a heavy cloak and hood, with one hand held to its chest and its face shadowed.
picture.credit: Claus de Werve (Netherlandish, 1380–1439), Mourner from the Tomb of Philip the Bold, Duke of Burgundy (1364–1404), 1404–10. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: Which early 20th-century German style is this bold, brightly colored painting of wrestlers?
items.explain: The painting is Wrestlers in a Circus (1909) by the German artist Ernst Ludwig Kirchner. Its harsh colors and distorted forms mark it as Expressionist, though the record itself does not name the style.

source.title: Wrestlers in a Circus, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: A large pink figure bent over in the foreground with a blue garment, set against flat areas of yellow, red, and green and dark figures in the background.
picture.credit: Ernst Ludwig Kirchner (German, 1880–1938), Wrestlers in a Circus, 1909. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: What is this seated portrait of a Buddhist monk mainly made of?
items.explain: The record gives the technique as Hinoki cypress wood with lacquer, metal staples and fittings. It is Japanese, Kamakura period.

source.title: Portrait of Hottō Enmyō Kokushi, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: A weathered, bald, elderly man in monk's robes sits on a low bench with hands folded in his lap, his surface worn and flaking.
picture.credit: Portrait of Hottō Enmyō Kokushi, c. 1295–1315. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: What is the figure of this robed mourner holding a book, carved from?
items.explain: The record gives the technique as salins alabaster. Jean de la Huerta carved it for a Burgundian tomb.

source.title: Mourner from the Tomb of John the Fearless and Margaret of Bavaria, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: A pale stone figure in a hooded monk's cloak holds a small book at its side and looks upward.
picture.credit: Jean de la Huerta (Spanish, active Burgundy, 1431–62), Mourner from the Tomb of John the Fearless and Margaret of Bavaria, 1443–45. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: What is the large winged figure in the left-hand painting of this open prayer book shown doing?
items.explain: The text on the right page begins with a prayer to Saint Michael the archangel. The record gives no description of the left-hand miniature, so the answer rests on the image.

source.title: Hours of Queen Isabella the Catholic, Queen of Spain, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: An open illuminated book. The left page shows a winged figure with a cross above fiery monsters, framed by flowers and insects on blue. The right page shows text.
picture.credit: Master of the First Prayerbook of Maximillian (Flemish, c. 1444–1519); Associates, Hours of Queen Isabella the Catholic, Queen of Spain, c. 1500. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: Who painted this sunlit landscape of the Roman countryside?
items.explain: The record credits La Cervara, the Roman Campagna to Corot, c. 1830–31.

source.title: La Cervara, the Roman Campagna, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: A dry, hilly landscape with pale cliffs, bare trees, a horseman and people on a dirt path, and cattle in the middle distance beneath a blue sky.
picture.credit: Jean Baptiste Camille Corot (French, 1796–1875), La Cervara, the Roman Campagna, c. 1830–31. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: Which people of the ancient Andes made this wooden panel with red-painted figures and metal details?
items.explain: The record identifies it as the Backrest of a Litter from the Chimú people of the North Coast of the Central Andes.

source.title: Backrest of a Litter, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: A red-painted wooden panel with five relief figures with large crescent headdresses and shell-inlaid eyes, framed by scroll borders.
picture.credit: Backrest of a Litter, 1185–1275 (radiocarbon date, 95.4% probability). Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: Who sculpted this life-sized bronze of a standing nude young man with one arm raised to his head?
items.explain: The record credits The Age of Bronze (1875–76) to the French sculptor Auguste Rodin.

source.title: The Age of Bronze, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: A dark bronze statue of a nude young man standing with one arm bent over his head and the other raised at his side.
picture.credit: Auguste Rodin (French, 1840–1917), The Age of Bronze, 1875–76. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: What metal is this cup, shaped like a raft with a seated figure, made of?
items.explain: The record says the Raft Cup is hammered silver soldered together, with chased decoration.

source.title: Raft Cup, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: A shiny metal cup shaped like a gnarled, curving tree-trunk raft, with a small bearded figure sitting inside and raising one arm.
picture.credit: Zhu Bishan (Chinese, c. 1300–after 1362), Raft Cup, 1300s–1400s. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: Which format is this circular Renaissance painting of the Holy Family?
items.explain: The record describes the work as a painting in tempera and oil on wood by Filippino Lippi. The picture shows its round shape, which is called a tondo.

source.title: The Holy Family with Saint John the Baptist and Saint Margaret, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: A round painting in a gilded frame showing an older man, a woman in blue and red holding a child, a young kneeling boy, and another woman before a cityscape.
picture.credit: Filippino Lippi (Italian, c. 1457–1504), The Holy Family with Saint John the Baptist and Saint Margaret, c. 1488–93. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: This relief from a royal palace at Nimrud shows a winged protective being. Which culture made it?
items.explain: The record lists it as Neo-Assyrian, from the Northwest Palace at Nimrud in the reign of Ashurnasirpal II.

source.title: Saluting Protective Spirit, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: A stone relief of a bearded, winged figure in profile with one hand raised and the other holding a branch with flowers, with lines of writing across the body.
picture.credit: Saluting Protective Spirit, 883–859 BCE. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: Which decoration technique is used on this blue-and-white jar with lion-head handles?
items.explain: The record gives the technique as porcelain with underglaze painted decoration, from Jingdezhen, Yuan dynasty.

source.title: Jar with Lion-Head Handles, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: A white jar with a short neck and two small animal-head handles, painted all over in blue with flowers, leaf scrolls, and panels.
picture.credit: Jar with Lion-Head Handles, 1300s. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: In this painting of a reclining woman, what is falling from above into her hand?
items.explain: The title is Danaë, by Orazio Gentileschi, c. 1623. The picture shows coins falling toward her, which fits the myth of the golden shower.

source.title: Danaë, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: A woman reclines on a bed with white sheets, reaching up toward small things falling from above, as a winged child pulls a dark curtain.
picture.credit: Orazio Gentileschi (Italian, 1563–1639), Danaë, c. 1623. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: What is the large central figure on this cross-shaped panel painting, with small scenes beside the body?
items.explain: The title is Crucifix with Scenes of the Passion, a tempera and gold panel from Pisa, c. 1230–40.

source.title: Crucifix with Scenes of the Passion, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: A cross-shaped gold-edged panel with a long-limbed figure with arms outstretched, flanked by small framed scenes and figures at the arm ends.
picture.credit: Crucifix with Scenes of the Passion, c. 1230–40. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: What wood is this ornate, carved sideboard topped with an eagle made from?
items.explain: The record lists the technique as walnut. Joseph Alexis Bailly made the sideboard around 1855.

source.title: Sideboard, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: A tall, dark wooden cabinet with elaborate carving of game animals, fruit and grapes, small standing figures, and an eagle on top.
picture.credit: Joseph Alexis Bailly (American, 1825–1883), Sideboard, c. 1855. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: This lavish soup tureen, with a lid topped by a cluster of vegetables and game, was made in Paris in the 1730s. What material is it made of?
items.explain: The museum record lists this Paris tureen of 1735–38 by Juste-Aurèle Meissonnier and others as silver.

source.title: Covered Tureen on Stand (Pot-à-oille), Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: A shiny metal lidded tureen with swirling shell-like curves, sitting on a leaf-shaped stand and topped with sculpted vegetables and small animals.
picture.credit: Juste-Aurèle Meissonnier (French, 1695–1750); Pierre-François Bonnestrenne (French); Henry Adnet (French, 1745), Covered Tureen on Stand (Pot-à-oille), 1735–38. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: This gold-ground devotional panel shows a mother pressing her cheek to a child. Who is the artist?
items.explain: The record attributes this icon of the Virgin Eleousa, painted in tempera and gold on wood around 1425–50, to the Cretan painter Angelos Akotantos.

source.title: Icon of the Mother of God and Infant Christ (Virgin Eleousa), Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: A painted panel on a gold background showing a woman in a dark red veil tenderly holding a child, their faces touching.
picture.credit: Angelos Akotantos (Cretan, died 1450), Icon of the Mother of God and Infant Christ (Virgin Eleousa), c. 1425–50. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: This carved pillar with drinking scenes, women and musicians comes from Mathura. What is it made of?
items.explain: The record gives the technique as red sandstone, from Kushan-period Mathura in India.

source.title: Corner Railing Pillar with Drinking Scenes, Yakshis, and Musicians, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: A tall, weathered reddish stone pillar carved with many standing and seated figures stacked in tiers.
picture.credit: Corner Railing Pillar with Drinking Scenes, Yakshis, and Musicians, 100s CE. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: This colorful landscape of a mountain, painted in patches of blue, orange and green, is by which artist?
items.explain: The museum lists Mount Sainte-Victoire, c. 1904, oil on fabric, as by the French painter Paul Cezanne.

source.title: Mount Sainte-Victoire, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: A landscape of a pale blue mountain behind rounded green trees and orange earth, painted in broad, separate brushstrokes.
picture.credit: Paul Cezanne (French, 1839–1906), Mount Sainte-Victoire, c. 1904. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: This ornate earthenware cooking pot with flame-like rim decoration was made in Japan around 2500 BCE. Which period does it belong to?
items.explain: The record identifies this Fire-flame Cooking Vessel as Japanese earthenware of the Jōmon period.

source.title: Fire-flame Cooking Vessel (Ka'en Doki), Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: A tall, tapering clay vessel with a dramatic crown of curling, serrated projections around the rim and swirling relief patterns.
picture.credit: Fire-flame Cooking Vessel (Ka'en Doki), c. 2500 BCE. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: This 1864 portrait of a young girl in a gray dress with white sleeves, holding red flowers, is by which painter?
items.explain: The record lists Romaine Lacaux, 1864, oil on fabric, as by the French painter Pierre-Auguste Renoir.

source.title: Romaine Lacaux, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: A young girl with short brown hair sits in a chair, hands clasped over red flowers in her lap, in a gray dress with white puffed sleeves.
picture.credit: Pierre-Auguste Renoir (French, 1841–1919), Romaine Lacaux, 1864. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: In this dimly lit scene, the young Christ sits by a woman who rests her head on her hand while he works with a crown of thorns. Who painted it?
items.explain: The museum attributes Christ and the Virgin in the House at Nazareth, c. 1640, to the Spanish painter Francisco de Zurbarán.

source.title: Christ and the Virgin in the House at Nazareth, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: A dark room where a boy in blue sits holding a thorny wreath while a woman in a pink-red dress rests her head on her hand; two white doves and a vase of flowers are nearby.
picture.credit: Francisco de Zurbarán (Spanish, 1598–1664), Christ and the Virgin in the House at Nazareth, c. 1640. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: This small Neolithic carving of a seated figure with a horned, bovine head is made of which material?
items.explain: The record gives the technique as jade (nephrite), from Neolithic northeast China, probably Hongshan culture.

source.title: Amulet in the Form of a Seated Figure with Bovine Head, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: A small polished stone carving of a crouching figure topped by a head with two tall upright horns, in gray-green and dark tones.
picture.credit: Amulet in the Form of a Seated Figure with Bovine Head, c. 4700–2920 BCE. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: This tomb guardian with a fierce animal head and flame-like spikes is made of glazed earthenware in which three-color style?
items.explain: The record describes it as glazed earthenware, sancai (three-color) ware, from Tang dynasty China.

source.title: Tomb Guardian with Animal Head, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: A ceramic creature seated on a base, with a fierce face and tall spikes in green, amber, white and blue glazes.
picture.credit: Tomb Guardian with Animal Head, early 700s. Cleveland Museum of Art

items.question: This carved stone ballgame object with openwork scrollwork surrounding a standing figure comes from which region?
items.explain: The record identifies the Ballgame Palma as stone work in the Classic Veracruz style from Mexico's Gulf Coast, c. 900–1100.

source.title: Ballgame Palma, Cleveland Museum of Art

picture.alt: A paddle-shaped gray stone sculpture covered in interlaced scrolls, with a small standing figure with a plumed headdress at the center.
